newsitem.title: USA: Hayes to close Michigan steel wheel plant.
newsitem.headline: Hayes to close Michigan steel wheel plant.

text.p: Hayes Wheels International Inc said it will cease production at its Romulus, Michigan, manufacturing plant in 1997.
"The decision was based on the company's continuing efforts to rationalize excess steel wheel capacity and reduce costs resulting from current market trends," Hayes said.
The Romulus plant makes steel and fabricated aluminum wheels for North American original equipment manufacturers.

Over the past decade, use of aluminum wheels on North American vehicles has increased to 43 percent from 12 percent, the company said. "The Romulus plant's steel wheel production dropped significantly during that same time frame, which resulted in the Romulus plant operating at less than 40 percent of its potential capacity during 1996," Hayes said.
About 435 people are employed at the plant, including 60 salaried and 375 hourly workers, the company said.
Production at the plant is expected to cease in late 1997, with the total shutdown of the plant completed by the end of the year, the company said.

"We will now work with the union to structure a shutdown agreement," said Hayes chief executive Ron Cucuz. "Our goal is to provide employees with a fair and equitable agreement in this difficult situation."
Hayes makes steel and aluminum wheels, brake drums and rotors for the automotive and commercial highway markets.
